question: What exactly changes between multi-head, grouped-query, and multi-query attention?
claim: Multi-head, grouped-query, and multi-query attention differ only in how many key/value heads the query heads share: one each, one per group, or one for all.
form: sibling variants on identical coordinates; target: the key/value heads, action: count them and trace which query heads read each; juxtaposition, because the structure below the query row differs

nodes.label: Q_1 ... Q_4

focus: key/value heads and their fan-outs in every panel
hue_note: No hue: the semantic map has no meaning for key/value sharing, so ink versus ghost and the fan-out structure carry the difference.

forbidden_edges.why: query heads never exchange values; sharing is only through a key/value head
a group's key/value head serves only that group

canvas: which query heads read each key/value head
caption: four query heads and a group size of 2 are illustrative
the key/value cache per token scales with the number of key/value heads
query head count is unchanged across variants

Multi-head, grouped-query, and multi-query attention differ only in how many key/value heads the query heads share: one each, one per group, or one for all. Query heads (gray) sit at the same positions in every panel; each arrow is a key/value head read by a query head. Four query heads and groups of two are illustrative; the key/value cache stored per token shrinks in proportion to the number of key/value heads, here 4, 2, and 1.
